name: FPS Single Immediate Payment, Bank A customer to Bank B customer (both directly connected settling participants)

steps.action: Payer authenticates in Bank A's app; strong customer authentication applies (PSRs 2017 reg 100).
steps.controls: Strong customer authentication

steps.action: For a new or amended payee, Bank A sends a CoP request API call to Bank B, which responds peer to peer (no central hub).
steps.messageOrPayload: CoP API request and response (format not publicly specified)
steps.controls: Payee name check mandated by SD17

steps.system: Bank A fraud, AML and sanctions controls
steps.action: Bank A runs fraud, AML and sanctions controls (MLRs 2017, OFSI consolidated list); if it has reasonable grounds to suspect APP fraud by D+1 it may hold the payment to end of D+4.
steps.controls: MLRs 2017 CDD and monitoring; OFSI consolidated list screening; fraud hold
steps.timing: Hold decision by end of D+1; release no later than end of D+4
steps.failures: Payment held or refused on suspicion of fraud or sanctions match

steps.action: Limit checks: £1m scheme maximum, the PSP's own lower limit, and the sender's Net Sender Cap for the current settlement cycle.
steps.controls: Scheme limit, PSP limit, Net Sender Cap
steps.failures: Payment rejected if limit or cap exceeded

steps.action: Bank A debits the payer's account and submits the payment to the FPS central infrastructure.
steps.messageOrPayload: not publicly specified (message format not verified in sources opened)
steps.ledgerEffect: Payer deposit at Bank A debited (commercial bank money)

steps.action: The central infrastructure routes the payment to Bank B, which accepts or rejects it in real time; Bank B credits the payee, usually almost immediately.
steps.ledgerEffect: Payee deposit at Bank B credited (commercial bank money) before interbank settlement
steps.timing: Usually almost immediate; legal maximum end of D+1 (reg 86)

steps.actor: Bank of England; Bank A; Bank B
steps.action: At the next deferred net settlement cycle, the multilateral net positions of Bank A and Bank B are settled across their BoE accounts; prefunding in collateralisation accounts covers each net debit cap.
steps.ledgerEffect: Central bank money moves between Bank A and Bank B BoE accounts (net)
steps.controls: Prefunded collateral up to net debit cap
steps.timing: Three cycles per business day per BoE 2017 and 2018 documents (2026 times need verification)

steps.actor: Payer; Bank A; Bank B; FOS
steps.action: Exception path: if the payment was an APP scam, the payer claims from Bank A within 13 months; reimbursement due within 5 business days up to £85,000 per claim, cost split 50:50 between Bank A and Bank B; the payer can escalate to FOS (limit £455,000).
steps.ledgerEffect: Reimbursement credited to payer; cost shared between sending and receiving PSPs
steps.timing: Claim within 13 months; reimbursement within 5 business days
steps.failures: Gross negligence exception; excess up to £100 (not for vulnerable customers)

endState: Payee credited in commercial bank money within seconds; interbank obligation discharged later in central bank money at the next RTGS net settlement cycle, covered by prefunded collateral.
limitations: FPS message format, current 2026 settlement cycle times and primary source on FPS returns or recalls were not verified. Customer credit is synchronous while interbank settlement is batch.

name: UK card-present purchase on a UK-issued Visa debit card at a UK merchant

steps.action: Cardholder taps or inserts the card; terminal and acquirer build an authorisation request.
steps.messageOrPayload: not publicly specified (message format not specified in sources opened)

steps.action: The acquirer routes the authorisation via VisaNet to the issuer.
steps.controls: Visa Core Rules 7.3: routing, declines, response time limits

steps.action: The issuer checks status, funds and fraud and approves or declines; on approval it places a hold on available funds.
steps.ledgerEffect: Hold on cardholder available funds; no interbank funds move
steps.controls: Issuer status, funds and fraud checks

steps.action: Later, the merchant or acquirer submits the transaction for clearing (Visa Core Rules 7.5); interchange applies, capped at 0.2% for a domestic consumer debit card under the UK IFR.
steps.ledgerEffect: Clearing records create receivables and payables
steps.controls: UK IFR 0.2% cap on domestic consumer debit interchange

steps.actor: Visa; issuer and acquirer settlement banks; Bank of England
steps.action: Visa calculates net positions; sterling net settlement goes through RTGS in 24-hour cycles, weekend cycles settled next business day; issuer-side settlement banks pay and acquirer-side settlement banks receive.
steps.ledgerEffect: Central bank money moves from issuer-side to acquirer-side settlement banks (net)

steps.action: The issuer posts the cleared transaction to the cardholder account; the acquirer funds the merchant net of fees on contractual timing.
steps.ledgerEffect: Cardholder account debited; merchant account credited net of fees (commercial bank money)

steps.action: Exceptions: disputes or chargebacks under Visa rules section 11; for a credit card, CCA s75 gives joint liability for items above £100 and up to £30,000; escalation to FOS.
steps.ledgerEffect: Chargeback reverses acquirer and merchant credit

endState: Merchant funded in commercial bank money; interbank positions settled net in central bank money in RTGS; issuer has debited the cardholder.
limitations: Authorisation is synchronous and moves no funds; clearing and settlement are batch. Card message format, exact 2026 Visa settlement time, Mastercard UK settlement and acquirer-to-merchant funding norms are not sourced.

name: US card-not-present credit card purchase

steps.action: Card details submitted; authorisation request sent.
steps.messageOrPayload: not publicly specified (network formats; ISO 8583 not confirmed)
steps.controls: Merchant and PSP fraud screening; authentication per network rules

steps.action: Issuer approves or declines and places a hold against the credit line.
steps.controls: Issuer fraud controls; OFAC applies to all US persons

steps.action: Capture and submission of clearing records.
steps.ledgerEffect: Acquirer records receivable from network and payable to merchant
steps.controls: Clearing per Visa s.7.5

steps.action: Interchange and fees applied; net positions computed.
steps.ledgerEffect: Issuer posts purchase to cardholder credit account; issuer owes network; acquirer is owed
steps.controls: Credit interchange is network-set; Reg II caps apply only to covered debit issuers, not credit

steps.system: Interbank funding, typically by wire (specific settlement banks and timing not sourced)
steps.action: Net obligations funded.
steps.ledgerEffect: Reserve balances move between master accounts; final and irrevocable when credited
steps.controls: Fedwire hours 21:00 (prior day) to 19:00 ET

steps.action: Merchant paid net of fees.
steps.ledgerEffect: Merchant deposit account credited (commercial bank money)
steps.controls: Merchant reserves (not sourced)

steps.system: Reg Z dispute plus network dispute
steps.action: Chargeback branch: cardholder notifies issuer; issuer may raise a chargeback; acquirer debits merchant or represents.
steps.ledgerEffect: Disputed amount cannot be collected or reported delinquent during Reg Z investigation; chargeback reverses acquirer and merchant credit
steps.controls: Reg Z unauthorized use liability lesser of $50 or amount obtained; billing error notice within 60 days, acknowledge in 30 days, resolve in two billing cycles, max 90 days; claims and defenses for purchases over $50; Visa 10.1/10.2 EMV liability shift; Category 13 consumer disputes
steps.timing: Reg Z timelines as stated; network time limits not extracted

endState: Merchant funded in commercial bank money; issuer holds receivable from cardholder; interbank positions settled in central bank money. Debit-card variant: Reg E $50/$500 liability and 10-business-day error resolution (90 days for POS) replace Reg Z; Reg II routing and cap apply.
limitations: Only steps 1 to 2 are real-time and no step before interbank funding moves central bank money. Card message formats, settlement bank arrangements and timing, and network dispute time limits are not confirmed; step 6 is inference with no source; Mastercard not researched.

name: ACH credit payroll, with ACH debit return branch

steps.actor: Employer (non-consumer Originator); ODFI; possibly Third-Party Sender
steps.action: Payroll credit file submitted.
steps.ledgerEffect: ODFI debits or holds employer funds (practice not sourced)
steps.controls: Risk-based monitoring for unauthorized and False Pretenses entries (Phase 1 from 20 Mar 2026, Phase 2 from 19 Jun 2026); OFAC screening
steps.failures: File rejection; BEC or payroll diversion

steps.action: File transmitted, sorted and distributed to RDFIs.
steps.controls: Operator deadlines
steps.timing: Same Day deposit deadlines 10:30, 14:45, 16:45 ET; next-day deadlines through 02:15 ET

steps.action: Net settlement.
steps.ledgerEffect: ODFI master account debited, RDFI master accounts credited (central bank money)
steps.controls: Same Day limit $1M per payment
steps.timing: Same Day settlement 13:00, 17:00 or 18:00 ET; next-day 08:30 ET

steps.action: Credit posted to employee.
steps.ledgerEffect: Employee deposit balance increases (commercial bank money)
steps.controls: RDFI credit monitoring (Phase 1 RDFIs with 10M+ 2023 receipts from 20 Mar 2026; all from 19 Jun 2026); Reg CC: electronic payments available by the business day after receipt
steps.failures: R02 account closed, R03 no account, R04 invalid number: return within 2 banking days

steps.action: Debit return branch (e.g. consumer bill-pay debit): R01 insufficient funds within 2 banking days, or R10 unauthorized or not recognized within 60 calendar days (written statement requirement not confirmed).
steps.ledgerEffect: Settlement reversed: RDFI recovers from ODFI, ODFI debits Originator
steps.controls: Reg E $50/$500 liability and error resolution (10 business days, extendable to 45/90 with provisional credit)

endState: Employee credited in commercial bank money; interbank positions net settled in Reserve Bank accounts by the ACH Operator at fixed windows; returns follow Nacha timeframes.
limitations: Reg J subpart C excludes ACH from FedNow payment orders and Nacha says its fraud rules do not alter UCC 4A liability. Nacha file and record formats, Same Day ACH funds availability deadlines and EPN mechanics not sourced.

name: FedNow vs RTP instant credit transfer (comparison)

steps.action: Sender bank authenticates customer, screens fraud and OFAC, checks limits and debits customer.
steps.controls: FedNow account activity thresholds by segment since Jun 2025; network limit $10M on both rails (FedNow since 12 Nov 2025, RTP since 9 Feb 2025); OFAC

steps.action: FedNow validates and settles gross: reserve balances move from sender to receiver master account (or correspondents').
steps.ledgerEffect: Master account balances debited and credited; no prefunding
steps.controls: Reg J subpart C

steps.action: RTP validates and settles by adjusting both banks' positions in the joint account ledger.
steps.ledgerEffect: RTP ledger positions in the RTP Prefunded Balance Account at FRBNY (central bank money) reallocated
steps.controls: RTP Operating Rules (not opened)

steps.action: Receiving bank credits the beneficiary immediately (FedNow obligation under Reg J subpart C; RTP under RTP Rules).
steps.controls: FedNow: extra-review notice for suspected fraud or sanctions; RTP: immediate availability subject to limited exceptions; Reg E applies where EFTA applies (EFTA prevails over Reg J subpart C)

steps.action: RTP participants top up joint account positions 24x7 via FedNow LMTs from master accounts, and via Fedwire in Fedwire hours (mechanics not sourced).
steps.ledgerEffect: Master account balances move to or from the RTP joint account

steps.action: Exceptions: FedNow allows 60 calendar days to report unauthorized or erroneous orders; RTP uses a request-for-return-of-funds message (no sender recall).
steps.messageOrPayload: RTP request for return of funds (message name not confirmed)
steps.ledgerEffect: Any return is a new credit transfer back

endState: Both rails deliver instant, final credit push payments up to $10M with ISO 20022 messaging: FedNow settles each payment gross in master accounts without prefunding (Fed-operated, production since 20 Jul 2023, over 1,800 participants per secondary source); RTP settles on its own ledger against the prefunded joint account at FRBNY (TCH-operated, bank-owned, production since 2017, over 1,378 participants).
limitations: ISO 20022 message names and versions (pacs.008, pacs.002 etc.) not confirmed; RTP Operating Rules text not opened; FedNow participant count is from a secondary source.

name: SCT Inst, payer at a German bank, payee at a French bank, both TIPS DCA holders (alternative via RT1)

steps.action: Payer enters payee IBAN, name and amount.
steps.controls: User-set per-day or per-transaction instant limit (IPR Art 5a(6)); order above limit not executed

steps.actor: Payer PSP (Requesting PSP); payee PSP (Responding PSP)
steps.action: Payer PSP sends a VOP request; response match, close match (name shown), no match (warning) or not possible; payer may still proceed with liability shifting per Art 5c(8).
steps.messageOrPayload: EPC VOP API request and response (spec v1.1.1, ISO 20022 resource elements); not a pacs message
steps.controls: Free of charge; before authorisation; registration in EPC Directory Service

steps.action: Payer authorises with strong customer authentication (two or more of knowledge, possession, inherence; dynamic linking per recitals 95-96).
steps.controls: SCA under PSD2 Art 4(30)

steps.action: No per-transfer screening against EU targeted financial sanctions (Art 5d(2)); daily customer screening and on every new listing instead; other restrictive measures and AML monitoring still apply; TFR intra-EU data requirements.
steps.controls: IPR Art 5d daily screening; TFR Art 5 (account numbers or unique transaction identifier), Art 4 otherwise

steps.action: Payer PSP time-stamps and sends the payment to TIPS.
steps.messageOrPayload: pacs.008.001.08 (DS-02) with mandatory AccptncDtTm in milliseconds
steps.timing: IPR 10-second clock runs from receipt by payer PSP

steps.action: TIPS validates and reserves the amount on the payer PSP's TIPS DCA, then forwards to the payee PSP; from reservation the order is entered and irrevocable in TARGET.
steps.ledgerEffect: Funds reserved on payer PSP TIPS DCA (central bank money)
steps.failures: Insufficient DCA liquidity or unreachable BIC leads to rejection

steps.action: Payee PSP checks the payee account and returns a positive or negative confirmation; on negative, TIPS releases the reservation and the payer PSP informs the payer.
On positive reply TIPS settles: debit payer PSP TIPS DCA, credit payee PSP TIPS DCA, final and irrevocable, and confirms to both PSPs.
steps.messageOrPayload: not publicly specified (TIPS notification message versions not extracted)
steps.ledgerEffect: Central bank money moves from payer PSP DCA to payee PSP DCA
steps.timing: 99.99% of payments under 5 s; TIPS timeout value not publicly extracted

steps.action: Payee PSP credits the payee and makes funds available.
steps.ledgerEffect: Illustrative: payee PSP Dr TIPS DCA (asset), Cr customer deposit (liability)
steps.timing: Within 10 s of receipt time (IPR Art 5a(4)(c)); EPC scheme page: 9 s maximum execution

steps.action: Payer PSP receives confirmation and informs the payer; if no confirmation within 10 s it informs the payer free of charge and restores the account.
steps.ledgerEffect: Illustrative: Dr payer deposit, Cr TIPS DCA
steps.failures: No confirmation in 10 s: restore account (Art 5a(4)(e), 5a(5))

steps.action: Payer PSP replenishes its TIPS DCA from T2 on T2 business days; rule-based liquidity transfers decided Jan/Feb 2026; weekend window planned (no date).
Exceptions after settlement: recall by PSP or request for recall by originator; positive answer is a new reverse settlement (original not unwound); negative answer; status investigation.

steps.actor: EBA CLEARING (RT1); payer and payee PSPs
steps.action: Alternative: steps 5 to 8 run through RT1 instead; RT1 positions are funded with central bank money in TIPS (participant TIPS DCA or across RT1 and TIPS via the RT1 AS technical account); ACHs connect via the TIPS platform so RT1 participants can exchange SCT Inst with TIPS DCA holders.
steps.ledgerEffect: Cover moves between RT1 AS technical account and TIPS DCAs
steps.timing: RT1 inter-PSP processing averages just over 1 s

endState: Payee funds available within 10 s; interbank obligation discharged with finality in central bank money (TIPS DCA, or RT1 AS technical account backed by TIPS).
limitations: Ledger entries are illustrative, not from operator documentation. TIPS timeout, TIPS notification message variants, RT1 funding cycles and SCT Inst recall deadlines not sourced.

steps.controls: Holding limit (not set)

HYPOTHETICAL settlement on the centralised platform, which processes and verifies settlements and holdings.

steps.controls: Finality moment not confirmed in sources opened

steps.ledgerEffect: Digital euro converted to merchant bank deposit
steps.controls: Merchant fee cap

steps.action: HYPOTHETICAL offline P2P: details known only to payer and payee; PSPs see funding and defunding; Parliament position that a lost device means lost offline funds (secondary).

steps.system: Draft rulebook dispute and fraud processes
steps.action: HYPOTHETICAL: disputes and fraud handled under draft rulebook v0.91 Annex D2 #4 (risk and fraud) and #5 (dispute management).

steps.action: Uploads KYC to CKYCR within 10 days, flags OTP e-KYC, shares KYC identifier; keeps records 5 years.

name: Buy USD stablecoin on a regulated exchange via bank transfer, send to another wallet, redeem or off-ramp

steps.actor: User and regulated exchange (EU CASP, UK MLR-registered firm until Oct 2027, US money transmitter/broker, Singapore PSA licensee, India FIU-IND-registered VDASP)
steps.action: (Step 1) Onboarding: customer due diligence and KYC.
steps.messageOrPayload: Identity, beneficial owner, source of funds data
steps.controls: CDD/KYC; India triggers CDD at relationship start and for transactions of INR 50,000 or more or any international transaction; EU authorised CASPs must onboard with full AML/CFT.
steps.failures: Unauthorised CASPs in the EU had to cease business after 1 July 2026.

steps.system: Domestic rail (ACH/wire in US, Faster Payments in UK, SEPA/SCT Inst in EU, FAST/PayNow in SG, IMPS/NEFT/UPI where banks permit in India)
steps.action: (Step 2) Fiat funding: credit transfer to the exchange's client-money/omnibus account.
steps.ledgerEffect: Bank-ledger debit/credit; exchange internal ledger credits user USD/EUR balance.
steps.controls: Bank sanctions screening; R16 payment transparency for cross-border wires.
steps.timing: Finality per rail settlement rules (see us.md, uk.md, eu.md)
steps.failures: Non-USD fiat implies FX at the exchange, outside regulated FX settlement systems such as CLS (inference).

steps.system: Exchange internal matching engine and ledger
steps.action: (Step 3) Purchase: user buys USD stablecoin. Where the exchange lacks inventory it buys from the issuer via mint (exchange wires USD to the issuer reserve bank account; issuer mints to the exchange address).
steps.ledgerEffect: Off-chain only: internal ledger reallocates; exchange holds tokens in omnibus custodial wallets. A primary mint increases on-chain supply and reserves.
steps.controls: UK FCA best execution and market abuse regime from 25 Oct 2027; in the EU non-MiCA-compliant EMTs cannot be offered by CASPs (inference from MiCA Title IV); Singapore DPT providers may not market non-MAS-regulated coins to retail as 'stablecoins' (proposed); India 1% TDS on VDA transfer consideration.

steps.actor: Exchange (originating VASP) and recipient (beneficiary VASP or self-hosted wallet)
steps.action: (Step 4) Withdrawal to another wallet: exchange signs a token transfer from its hot wallet (key management via HSM/MPC, vendor-described).
steps.messageOrPayload: Travel Rule originator/beneficiary information sent off-chain to the beneficiary VASP (IVMS101 data model over a protocol)
steps.ledgerEffect: On-chain balance moves; exchange internal ledger debits user.
steps.controls: Sanctions screening of destination address and chain analytics risk scoring (vendor tools); EU ownership assessment for self-hosted wallets above EUR 1,000; FATF notes P2P/unhosted transfers are high risk and outside obliged-entity monitoring.
steps.timing: Chain-specific finality (Ethereum: finalised after checkpoint finalisation); beneficiary VASP credits after its own confirmation threshold.

steps.action: (Step 5) Hold or transfer between self-hosted wallets.
steps.controls: Issuer can freeze or blacklist addresses on authority request.

steps.actor: Issuer (onboarded institutional customer; retail typically redeems via intermediary) and issuer's reserve custodian/bank
steps.action: (Step 6a) Redemption via issuer: holder sends tokens to the issuer redemption address; issuer burns; issuer pays fiat from the reserve account over a bank rail.
steps.ledgerEffect: On-chain supply reduced (burn); reserve assets reduced (sale of T-bills or deposit drawdown); bank ledger credit to redeemer.
steps.controls: US proposed redemption within two business days, minimum one coin; EU EMT holders have a par claim; UK systemic within 24 hours; UK FCA KYC before redemption period.
steps.timing: US proposal: generally within two business days; UK systemic: real time or within 24 hours. Finality: burn on-chain plus fiat-rail finality.
steps.failures: Issuer-specific minimums (for example Circle Mint account thresholds) not verified.

steps.system: Public blockchain, exchange internal ledger, bank rail
steps.action: (Step 6b) Off-ramp via exchange: user deposits stablecoin to the exchange (Travel Rule inbound checks, chain analytics on source), sells for fiat and withdraws by bank transfer.
steps.messageOrPayload: Travel Rule inbound data (not further specified)
steps.ledgerEffect: On-chain deposit; internal ledger; bank-rail payout.
steps.controls: India: 30% tax on gains and 1% TDS apply. Mainland China: fiat-crypto exchange is an illegal financial activity, so no lawful onshore off-ramp exists.
steps.failures: Mainland China: no lawful onshore off-ramp.

endState: User holds fiat again (via issuer redemption or exchange off-ramp); tokens either burned (issuer redemption, reserves reduced) or transferred to the exchange (secondary market, reserves unchanged). The trace crosses three ledgers (user bank, exchange internal ledger, public blockchain) and up to four regulated actors.
limitations: Where the US regime is referenced, GENIUS-specific requirements are proposals not yet effective. Rail finality is in country files. HSM/MPC key management and chain analytics are vendor-described. Issuer-specific redemption terms (Circle, Paxos, Tether) not verified. FX at the on-ramp and some controls are inferences.
